extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, petitioners, patent owners, and parties practicing before the PTAB
extracted.subtask_short: inter partes and post-grant review rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedural rules and substantive filing/institution standards for inter partes review (IPR) and post-grant review (PGR) proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), covering eligibility, timing, petition content, service, institution standards, amendments, supplemental information, joinder, and related trial deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial procedure and pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes review or post-grant review is a trial subject to the procedures in subpart A and shall be administered such that pendency before the Board after institution is normally no more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency may be extended by up to six months for good cause by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge, or adjusted by the Board in the case of joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in an unexpired patent shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the patent in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction rule applies to both inter partes review and post-grant review proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may petition for inter partes review (eligibility / bars)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner of a patent may file a petition for inter partes review unless: (a) before filing the petition the petitioner or real party-in-interest filed a civil action challenging the patent; (b) the petition is filed more than one year after the petitioner (or real party-in-interest or privy) was served with an infringement complaint; or (c) the petitioner (or real party-in-interest or privy) is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are jurisdictional/eligibility bars for filing an IPR petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may petition for post-grant review (eligibility / bars)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner of a patent may file a petition for post-grant review unless: (a) before filing the petition the petitioner or real party-in-interest filed a civil action challenging the patent; or (b) the petitioner (or real party-in-interest or privy) is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR does not include the IPR one-year-served limitation; estoppel and prior civil action bars still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing — inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for inter partes review must be filed after the later of: (1) nine months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent; or (2) if a post-grant review is instituted, the date of termination of such post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may also impose limits on the number of inter partes reviews instituted during the first four one-year periods after the statutory change by notice in the Official Gazette or Federal Register; petitions filed after a set limit will be untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing — post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for post-grant review must be filed no later than nine months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent (with special rules for reissues identical/narrower than original patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may impose limits on the number of PGRs instituted during each of the first four one-year periods; petitions after a limit are untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and payment for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescribed fee (IPR fee under § 42.15(a) or PGR fee under § 42.15(b)) must accompany the petition, and no filing date will be accorded until full payment is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is required to obtain a filing date; failure to pay delays or prevents obtaining a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of petition — grounds for standing
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must certify that the patent is available for the requested review and that the petitioner is not barred or estopped from requesting review on the grounds identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is a required standing statement for both IPR and PGR petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of petition — identification of challenge (IPR specific required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each challenged claim the petition must identify: (1) the claim; (2) the specific statutory grounds under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 and the patents or printed publications relied upon for each ground; (3) how the challenged claim is to be construed (including identification of corresponding specification portions for 112(f) limitations); (4) how the construed claim is unpatentable and where each element is found in the prior art; and (5) exhibit numbers of supporting evidence and the relevance/identification of specific portions relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where a party fails to state its relevance or to identify specific supporting portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of petition — identification of challenge (PGR specific required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each challenged claim the petition must identify: (1) the claim; (2) the specific statutory grounds permitted under 35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3) on which the challenge is based; (3) how the claim is to be construed (including 112(f) identification); (4) how the construed claim is unpatentable (for prior-art grounds, specify where each element is found; for other grounds, identify the specific part of the claim that fails and explain why); and (5) exhibit numbers and relevance with specific portions identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with IPR, the Board may exclude evidence lacking a stated relevance or specific citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to correct clerical or typographical mistakes in petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion may be filed to correct clerical or typographical mistakes in the petition, and grant of such a motion does not change the filing date of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical corrections are allowed but do not affect the petition's filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must serve the petition and exhibits on the patent owner at the correspondence address of record; petitioner may additionally serve at other known addresses likely to effect service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service may be electronic upon agreement of parties; service may be by EXPRESS MAIL® or by means at least as fast and reliable as EXPRESS MAIL®; personal service is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements — complete versus incomplete petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition will not be accorded a filing date until it (1) complies with the content requirements, (2) effects service on the correspondence address of record, and (3) is accompanied by the required fee. If incomplete, the Office will dismiss the petition if the deficiency is not corrected within one month from the notice of an incomplete petition (or, for PGR, earlier of one month or the statutory deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete petitions receive no filing date and face dismissal unless promptly corrected per the one-month cure period (subject to statutory deadline for PGR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response by patent owner — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response limited to reasons why no review should be instituted under the pertinent statute (35 U.S.C. 314 for IPR, 324 for PGR). The preliminary response can include evidence except it shall not present new testimonial evidence beyond that already of record (except as authorized by the Board). It may not include any amendment and is subject to page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response is due no later than three months after notice that the petition has been accorded a filing date; a patent owner may waive the preliminary response by election to expedite the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer of claims by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a statutory disclaimer under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) disclaiming one or more claims in the patent; no review will be instituted based on disclaimed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a statutory disclaimer is an available tactic to remove claims from the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board institution discretion and partial institution
rubrics_metrics.description: When instituting review, the Board may authorize review to proceed on all or some of the challenged claims and on all or some of the grounds of unpatentability asserted for each claim. At any time prior to institution, the Board may deny some or all grounds for some or all challenged claims; denial of a ground is a decision not to institute on that ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution can be partial (claims/grounds) and the Board may narrow institution before formally instituting a trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard — inter partes review (reasonable likelihood)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review shall not be instituted for a ground of unpatentability unless the Board decides that the petition would demonstrate a reasonable likelihood that at least one of the claims challenged is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board’s institution decision will take into account any patent owner preliminary response where filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard — post-grant review (more likely than not)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review shall not be instituted for a ground of unpatentability unless the Board decides that the petition would, if unrebutted, demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least one challenged claim is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board’s decision will consider any patent owner preliminary response. Additionally, novel or unsettled legal questions important to other patents or applications may establish sufficient grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response after institution
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, a patent owner may file a response addressing any ground for unpatentability not already denied; the response is filed as an opposition and is subject to page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no Board order sets a due date, the default due date is three months from the date the review was instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — one motion and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file one motion to amend a patent, but only after conferring with the Board. Unless a due date is provided by Board order, the motion must be filed no later than the filing of the patent owner response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion to amend may be denied if it does not respond to a ground of unpatentability or if it seeks to enlarge claim scope or introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption on number of substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend may cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims. The presumption is that only one substitute claim would be needed to replace each challenged claim, which may be rebutted by demonstration of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumptive one-for-one substitution can be rebutted with evidence demonstrating need for more substitute claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for motion to amend claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend must include a claim listing, show changes clearly, and set forth: (1) the support in the original disclosure for each claim added or amended; and (2) the support in any earlier-filed disclosure for any claim for which benefit of that filing date is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating written description/support in the original disclosure (and earlier disclosures where priority is asserted) is required to justify claim amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional motion to amend — Board authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional motion to amend beyond the one permitted may not be filed without Board authorization. Additional motions may be authorized for good cause or by joint request of the parties to materially advance a settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding whether to authorize an additional motion the Board will consider whether a petitioner submitted supplemental information after the time period set for filing a motion to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple proceedings, stay, transfer, consolidation, termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where another matter involving the patent is before the Office, the Board may during the pendency of the review enter any appropriate order regarding the additional matter, including stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board has broad case management authority to coordinate related Office matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder may be requested by a patent owner or petitioner; any request for joinder must be filed as a motion under § 42.22 no later than one month after the institution date of the inter partes review for which joinder is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-year-time limit of § 42.101(b) does not apply when the petition is accompanied by a request for joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing supplemental information after institution — timely and late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a trial is instituted, a party may file a motion to submit supplemental information if: (1) a request for authorization is made within one month of the date the trial is instituted; and (2) the supplemental information is relevant to a claim for which the trial has been instituted. For supplemental information more than one month after institution, a party must request authorization and show why the information reasonably could not have been obtained earlier and that consideration is in the interests-of-justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental information not relevant to instituted claims requires authorization with the same showing of inability to obtain earlier and interests-of-justice justification.
